content:
Sara McNamara recently asked me how i define AI native.

And since then i've been turning the term over in my head again and again.
I think it gets thrown around pretty generously, with very little explanation of what it ACTUALLY means, especially in RevOps.

Almost every RevOps leader i talk to uses AI now. Call summaries and email drafts are pretty much everywhere.

That's using AI. It's not the same thing as being AI native.

My take is that AI native is an approach to a problem, not a tool habit. AI lets us solve complex problems easier and faster than ever before. So if a leader is heavily using AI to knock out core GTM challenges, to me they're AI native.

The part i keep coming back to is the word core.

Writing a faster follow-up email isn't a core GTM challenge. A forecast nobody trusts is. So is a pipeline full of deals with close dates from last quarter, or a plan that's already stale by the time it ships, or the internal tool that never gets built because nobody has the time.

The AI-assisted version of RevOps does the same work a little faster. The AI-native version asks whether that work needs to exist in the shape it's in today.

i'm guilty of stopping at the 2nd more often than i'd like.

The slide is my rough attempt at the difference across a few areas of RevOps. It's a starting point, not a finished definition.

Curious on how others in Revops are defining 'AI native'

In a modern GTM motion, buyers don’t follow a clean, linear path.

They lean on trusted voices like partners, communities, advisors - before they talk to Sales, especially when the internet is full of information overload. 

So if your RevOps engine isn't set up to support Partner Ops, you're missing the mark.

✅ Clear attribution between partner-sourced and influenced deals
✅ Faster deal velocity (20–30% faster in some models)
✅ Higher ACVs due to trust-led influence
✅ Visibility into which partners actually drive revenue
✅ Scalable onboarding, enablement, and compensation workflows

Partner Ops isn’t just “a nice to have” - It’s a revenue multiplier!

But most teams struggle with:
❌ No PRM in place (or using one like a folder structure)
❌ Chaotic partner tagging and late-stage attribution
❌ Comp plans that pit sales and partnerships against each other
❌ Zero visibility into what happens after a referral

Everyone thinks RevOps is all about:
• Process optimization
• Data analysis
• Running CRM

(And yes, those matter!)

But if you've been in RevOps for more than a minute...
You know there's a lot more happening behind the scenes.

On any given day,  you're wearing 5 invisible hats:

1. The Therapist
 ↳ SDRs vent about lead quality
 ↳ Sales feels the process is too strict
 ↳ Marketing wants better attribution
 ↳ CS just wants something to work
You’re the safe space. The listener. The RevOps counselor.

2. The Coach
 ↳ You guide, clarify, and motivate
 ↳ You give feedback, tough love, real talk
 ↳ You make sure everyone’s playing the same game
You’re not just setting up CRM fields. You’re coaching the team to win.

3. The Negotiator
 ↳ Sales wants full lead control
 ↳ Partners want tighter handovers
 ↳ Leadership wants results now
 ↳ Finance wants less spending
You’re the middle ground. The peacekeeper.  The one who aligns everyone with the bigger picture.

4. The Detective
 ↳ CRM data doesn’t match the report?
 ↳ Something feels “off”?
 ↳ Someone shouts "the leads disappeared!"?
 ↳ The forecast moved!
You’re on it. Sherlock of the stack.

5. The Project Manager
 ↳ New tool rollout?
 ↳ Pipeline restructuring?
 ↳ Team training?
You own it. Timelines, tasks, follow-ups — all you. And most of the times with 0 formal project management training! 

So next time someone asks “what does RevOps really do?”

When successful startups launch a product, they really get to know who they're really making it for. They shape and tweak their offerings based on real feedback, always aiming to get closer to their customers’ true needs. 

This isn't just smart and effective for products, but also incredibly relevant and transformative for #RevOps when rolling out a new process or tool.  

Here's why I think treating RevOps as an in-house startup could be a game-changer:

👥 Get to Know Your Teams: Jump into the deep end to understand what makes your GTM teams tick—their workflow snags, their frustrations, and all the little things that could make or break their day. It's about getting the full picture right from the start and learning about their pain points as discovery is a key step before creating any process.

🤝 Build It Together: From day one, bring your teams into the conversation. Their insights are gold. By really listening and taking their feedback into account, you're not just crafting solutions for them but with them, paving the way for smoother adoption in the end.

🔎 Test and Learn: Grab a diverse mix of folks to test your new ideas or tools (different segments, different personalities). It isn't about getting it perfect right off the bat but learning from their experiences to refine your approach.

🤘 Support All the Way: When it’s time to hit the "go" button, back it up with solid documentation and how-tos (put it in your LMS or make a loom). It's about more than just getting everyone on board; it's about giving them what they need to really make these changes successful.

🎉 Communicate and Celebrate: Make the launch of new processes an event! Clear communication (post in slack channels or join standups). This along with visible support from leadership can underscore its importance and encourage adoption.

🗣 Keep the Conversation Going: The journey doesn't end at launch. Keep the lines of feedback open to tweak, adjust, and perfect your processes. It's all about staying agile and responsive ensuring that your processes remain flexible enough to move with the growth of the org. 

📈 Encourage Adoption, Measure the Wins: For RevOps to truly hit its stride, just like a startup, it needs its 'customers'—in this case, your GTM team—to not just try out but fully embrace the new processes and tools. This means engaging with them continuously, proving the real benefits, and adjusting based on what they say works (or doesn't). To do that, understand the baseline to make your impact measurable. 

Treating RevOps like its own vibrant startup within your org isn't just about shaking up processes; it's about fostering a culture of innovation, efficiency, and shared success. It’s about making sure RevOps isn’t just supporting but leading your GTM teams to achieve amazing things.

Does your CRM look like this when your admin is on PTO or leaves altogether? 🧐

it shouldn’t ... 🙅🏽‍♂️ 

A well designed CRM architecture should not go down the drain with one person. Most founders and CEOs I talk to are completely unaware of risk that can lead to major hurdles to the GTM motion.

Here are 5 Best Practices I like to use to ensure that your CRM is resilient and not dependent on a single admin:

1️⃣ Document Everything: Create a comprehensive knowledge base with detailed processes, workflows, and configurations. Use tools like Notion, Confluence or even Google Drive to make documentation accessible to the team.

2️⃣ Cross-Train Your Team: Identify a backup admin or train team members on key CRM functions. Even basic training for your marketing, sales, and service teams can empower them to handle common tasks on their own.

3️⃣ Standardize Processes: Implement clear naming conventions, folder structures, and automation rules so others can easily understand your CRM setup. You have no idea how happy it makes someone investigating what is going on, to read a clear flow description. Consistency reduces confusion in times of transition.

4️⃣ Audit Your System Regularly: Perform quarterly or semi-annual audits to identify potential single points of failure. Use these audits to validate workflows, security settings, and data integrity.

5️⃣ Use Managed Services: Partner with experts like RevInfinity (shameless plug 💁🏽‍♂️) to ensure continuity during transitions, leaves, or turnover. Having a trusted partner who knows your CRM well means you’re never left without support.

The urge to vibe code every GTM tool in your stack is very real. I'm guilty of it — as a builder, I feel like a kid in a candy shop.

But after 10 years of building and launching RevOps initiatives, there are a few things I'm seeing a lot of people skip over.

Every tool you vibe code comes with hidden costs. The launch is exciting. It may even get you a shoutout in the company slack. But real challenges bubble up when you put the solution out there in the world — and most teams skip planning for this.

They account for 10% of costs. The other 90% shows up later, after you're already too committed to stop.

The 10% you plan for:
- Build time (4–6 weeks) - in some cases 2-4!
- Tokens
- One technical SME

The 90% that gets you:
- Upstream API and model changes — every update is now your problem
- Scope creep — one use case becomes five
- Data model drift and versioning — your model moves, someone has to update the tool
- Bug fixes — you are the support + product + CS team
- Single-person knowledge risk — builder leaves, you start over
- Rep adoption and training — never in the original estimate, age long RevOps problem that doesn't just go away

This is what the build vs buy conversation is actually about. Not the build. The ownership.

It's 2024, you lift up a rock and there is a new GTM tool selling you the magic potion that will solve all your business problems…. 🤦‍♂️

Having evaluated hundreds of such tools in my RevOps career, here are the top 4 pieces of advice I would give to every Revenue/GTM leader out there looking to add to their tech stack:

1) All that glitter is not gold 
Do not just go for the shiniest new tool on the market because someone shared a LinkedIn post about how amazing it was for them, including this one 👀 (your org’s problems, capabilities, or timing might not be the same for it to work well). Do your thorough research and see if it fits the needs of your current business well and if it actually solves any of the real challenges your teams are having.

2) Go beyond the features list
The ever-growing feature list for these tools is head-spinning at times and it will only get larger with time. Your conversational intelligence tool will tell you that they also do outbound calling now, and your outbound calling tool will tell you that they also do forecasting now, and on top conversational intelligence too 🤯 Just because they do it doesn’t mean they do it well! You probably wouldn’t go to Domino’s for a burger if they told you they added it to their menu. You need to narrow down to the core competencies of that product and align with your need.

3) Be future-forward
Ask yourself if you stayed with this tool, will you need to shop around for a different one 3 years down the line? If the answer is no, sign a multi-year deal and bring your costs down. Be strategic instead of reactive, and keep in mind that the migration costs down the line will be much higher than today, as a badly done change management can be very costly.

4) Find a partner, not a service provider
There are so many great companies out there that have a customer-first philosophy. These companies truly become partners with you and are willing to take the work off your plate (in a startup there is nothing better than someone taking the stress of implementing and enabling your GTM team). Quarterly account reviews from such partners also keep your goals aligned.

Here are some of the best partners I have worked with in terms of tech stack and would recommend: Chili Piper, Salesloft, Clay, 6sense 👌🏽

Here are the worst ones: Linkedin Sales Navigator, Zoominfo, and Outreach 😑 (Will spare them the tag as the goal is awareness not ridicule)

As we wrap 2025, I wanted to share a few RevOps highlights I’m especially proud of.

This was the year we built the machine behind Unify's growth.

And the wild part?
We did it all in 6 months!!

Here’s what stood out:

(1) We doubled ARR. Yes, doubled!
Our GTM machine is not only tighter, it's more accountable and more predictable with 6 consecutive record breaking ARR months.

Not by coincidence, but by engineered growth.

(2) Forecast accuracy jumped from 50% to 90%!
It’s no longer a guessing game. 
It’s a tightly run process led by RevOps with 3 layers of accountability. 

(3) Win rates climbed by 10%.
We launched new qualification frameworks (SPICED + BANT) and prioritized quality over quantity. 

(4) We built real-time CRM hygiene.
We deployed AI agents that auto de-dupe accounts and contacts in Salesforce.
No more Slacks to RevOps asking for merges.

(5) Scored entire database in our CRM + New ICP scoring that happens in real time!
Every new Account is enriched with 10+ data points and scored in our CRM before reps even see it.

(6) $52M in qualified pipeline created.
 Nearly 20% came from Unify’s own automated outbound engine.
 The machine is generating its own fuel.

(7) 40+ hours/month saved through automation.
We eliminated repetitive workflows by deploying Agents across the most redundant tasks.
One example: an agent for pre-call prep for our AEs

(8) RevOps delivered intelligence, not just data.
 We gave leadership real insights with clear recommendations:
 → At what stage conversions drop and why
 → What is our winning channel and why we win there
 → Early signals of slowdown in Pipeline and what to do 
 → How well is our new products performing and why
 → What products gaps are contributing to close lost 
 Data alone doesn’t help leadership, you have to be able to tell a story. 

All of it worked because the data foundations were solid.
We didn’t rush. We built it right.

2025 wasn’t about flashy dashboards or copied 30-step N8N workflows from someone's Linkedin.

It was about turning RevOps into a machine that drives growth end to end and then layering AI on top to supercharge it. That is how modern RevOps should be  in today's world.

To more building in 2026.

Companies today are rewriting the Revenue playbook 📕  

Efficiency, Transparency, Accountability, Predictability — these are the new superheroes, from the boardroom all the way to the frontlines of Sales.

The era of mindless growth is long gone, and the age of wide scale optimization is here. That is precisely why RevOps is on the rise 🚀  

For those still questioning its ROI or grasping what RevOps even does, let me break it down with a simple analogy:

Think of departments such as Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partnerships as islands. People on these islands are usually busy in their day-to-day lives, operating completely in silos to achieve individual goals. Sales hustles to close deals, Marketing juggles campaigns and conferences, Partnerships forges connections, and Customer Success aims for satisfaction while reducing churn. Enter RevOps. 

RevOps is the bridge that connects these islands (cross-functional) and teaches them to speak the same language (common metrics) to maximize synergy and efficiency. This, in turn, reduces costs for everyone involved and creates global alignment, with everyone striving to achieve the same goals. That is RevOps and that is its ROI in simple terms.

⚠️ Your CRM data is not safe anymore by default ⚠️ 

2 months ago Salesforce quietly had all its customers Opt in to use their customer data to train their AI models. Today HubSpot pulled a similar shady move, informing customers that their data can be shared with other customers (yup you read that right) and will be used by HubSpot to train their AI models.

Here is why this is a big issue:

1. These comms are buried into regular email updates or in change logs. This isn't a conversation that your AM is having with you and neither is a more publicly announced move. Its super easy to miss and that is by design. This erodes all the trust.

2. To double down on the trust deficit: The default for this isn't Opt out, its Opt it!! The settings are buried deep into your CRM managed by admins to go find and toggle it off (see below how you can do it). 

3. Using customer data to train their LLM models while the entire AI industry is running on no guardrails is absurd!

Here's how to Opt out (You need to be super admin to do so):
Salesforce: Settings > Opt Out of Customer Data Access > Toggle Off
HubSpot: Settings  > AI > AI model training > Toggle Off

If you are in RevOps and have the keys to your company CRM, go in and make these updates.

This is the new playbook. assume every vendor will do this next. assume the default is unsafe. assume you have to hunt for the opt-out.

content:
We've started to blame the agents.

After being close to autonomous agent deployment for months, I'm starting to hear this more often:

"It just started doing that" 
"Must have hallucinated" 
"The MCP connection broke"

But good Revenue leaders have never accepted that as an answer to a broken process.

Agents break. That part isn't surprising. The shift is that we've started talking about them like they're the ones responsible, and the org still holds a human accountable anyway.

That's always been the deal in RevOps. When the pipeline's clean, automations fire and routing works, RevOps becomes invisible. The month a scoring model drifts and sales chases the wrong accounts for three weeks, you are the topic of conversation.

Today the blame is deflected towards the agent. The accountability still lands on you.

There's an old IBM training line from 1979 that reads differently today:
 "A computer can never be held accountable, therefore a computer must never make a management decision."

Autonomous agents are the first time that rule gets tested outside a hypothetical. My take: the rule still holds. The agent makes the call, you still answer for it. What changes is the weight: one operator now stands behind a growing pile of decisions they didn't personally make, and only hears about the ones that broke.

So the future operator isn't the one running the most agents. It's the one who can still answer for every one of them: what it's doing, when it last drifted, how they'd know if it failed tonight and whats the plan to fix it. 

Curious to hear how others operators have experienced this?

content:
It's great to see that many companies today are jumping onto the RevOps bandwagon 🚀 

But, let's be honest, there's still a fair bit of ambiguity out there, which begs Go-to-Market (GTM) leaders to ask the critical question: Are we really on the right track? 🤔 

While we may not get the answer to that right away, I believe the right strategy behind the RevOps function can significantly influence your org's trajectory, regardless of size or whether resources are invested internally or externally.

Here are a few key areas to keep in mind:

1) Understanding the Maturity Cycle: Having an understanding of your org's stage is crucial — whether you're starting up, scaling up, or IPO-ready? This awareness helps guide where you needs to focus and spend more time. Will RevOps prioritize building? or will they focus to maximize current synergies? This will help align your current and future needs.

2) GTM Strategy: Your RevOps should align with your GTM approach. Whether it's product-led, sales-driven, or a hybrid, the nature of your GTM motion dictates the skill sets and focus areas your RevOps should have to effectively support and enhance the org.

3) Predictability in Deal Velocity and Size: If you are dealing with unpredictability in transaction volumes or sales cycles, the right RevOps team should bring a level of predictability crucial for the strategic planning. Whether dealing with transactional sales or navigating long cycles with high Average Contract Value (ACV), forecasting and optimization are paramount to success. 

4) Data Insights and Infrastructure: A subpar infrastructure will hinder your ability to gather actionable insights from your data. A world-class RevOps team should not only excel in data analysis but also in enhancing data governance, hygiene, and architecture. Without this in place your forecast will always be untrustworthy. 

5) System Expertise: This is more of a ‘duh’. Employ individuals with a strong grasp of the tools in place, from your CRM to any other systems utilized for GTM, as this expertise can serve as an accelerator to your goals. 

6) The Power of 'No': Lastly, your RevOps need to have a remarkable ability to prioritize. Often, that will mean challenging decisions and offering strategic alternatives rather than consenting to every directive. This skill serves as a testament to their focus on what genuinely matters. 

These areas can serve as a strategic framework to ensure RevOps is equipped to help the org win and may help navigate some uncharted waters.

(If you’re a RevOps or GTM leader, this one’s for you)

Software buying used to be strategic.

Now?

It feels like navigating a maze.
Every tool wants to do everything.

But when every platform blends into the next → how do you know what it’s actually good at?

Here’s what’s driving the blur:
AI & Low Code Boom 
↳ Tools can now spin up new features fast 
↳ Niche tools suddenly feel like “platforms”

Budget Cuts = Stack Consolidation 
↳ Leaders are under pressure to “do more with less” 
↳ One “super-tool” to replace five niche apps? Tempting. Finance loves it.

Differentiation = Foggy Concept 
↳ Sales, CS, analytics, marketing… all bundled in one (Throw in slack too, why not!?)
↳ But what’s the core value anymore?

So… how do you actually choose the right tool?

Here’s my short list to cut through the noise:
→ Start with your non-negotiables - Don’t get sold on flashy features. Solve your core problems first.
→ Use cases > features Ask real users. Test real workflows. Ignore the brochure and flashy feature set
→ Test with your process -  Not their data. Not their demo. Your setup. Your workflows. Your data.
→ Prioritize integrations -  If it doesn’t fit your stack? It’s just more work. Avoid!
→ Check for scalability - Will this tool still solve the problem you are going to be solving in 12 months? 24?

Final thought: This trend isn’t slowing down. SaaS platforms will keep blending in coming years. 

It’s on RevOps to stay focused, be discerning, and choose tools that truly move the needle.

It's 2025 and it’s great to see so many large and small companies realizing that RevOps is not only a nice to have anymore, its a core function that is necessary for success.  

But let’s be real, the more I talk to leaders looking to add RevOps firepower the more i realize that there is still a fair bit of ambiguity on what they want out of it and how to set this function up for success. 

Here is my take on it. RevOps is not a quick fix, and it definitely is not a one-size-fits-all solution. Before jumping on the bandwagon and expecting instant results, here are a few key areas I always advise businesses/leaders to keep in mind:

➡️  Define clear objectives:
There are a million things RevOps can focus on, so as a business your RevOps should have very clearly defined objectives that they are working towards in the short, medium and long term. Else all you are doing is dumping on a list of responsibilities and expecting these areas to be magically be fixed one by one. The more specific your goals, the better the outcomes. 

➡️ Understand the maturity of your org before you expect results:
A startup needs RevOps to build foundational processes, so give them the autonomy to do so and expect a shakeup in things as they build. On the other hand a scaling/established business needs to optimize and refine, so expect incremental improvements to ongoing areas instead of an overnight overhaul. Have your RevOps be aligned to where you are today and prep them for where you want to go.

➡️ Know how RevOps supports your GTM motion:
Your RevOps function should align with how you sell. A product-led business needs automation and deep analytics focus closely working with the product team, while a sales-led motion relies on standard pipeline management, account based marketing/strategy and deal desk efficiency etc. The wrong focus can slow things down, and handicap your RevOps.

➡️  Invest in the right tools, but prioritize strategy:
Tech stacks don’t solve problems on their own. A messy CRM or unstructured data won’t magically improve just because you add more tools. If that is the case then give your RevOps time to focus on strategy first, then layer in the right systems to support it. 

➡️ Give RevOps a seat at the table:
Too often, RevOps is treated as an afterthought rather than a strategic partner. To truly drive impact, RevOps leaders need to be part of your key GTM discussions and decision-making, not just fixing broken processes in the background and spinning up reports when you have a board meeting. 

RevOps, when done right, can transform how a business operates. But it requires clarity, alignment, and investment in the right areas.

content:
For RevOps there has been no better time to build than today.

But where I see a bunch of folks getting stuck: troubleshooting.

Most of us were trained to ask simple questions because search engines like Google rewarded it. AI doesn't.

All the workflows I built in early testing underperformed compared to what I run today. It had nothing to do with the AI. It was the prompt.

After numerous iterations, here's where I landed — 4 parts (using a real example):

Intent — the outcome + stakes. Not "analyze pipeline." Try: "I have a forecast call with leadership Thursday. I don't want to be blindsided — I need to know where we stand on pipeline, risks, and gaps before I walk in."

Action — what to pull from and write to. Calendar, Salesforce, Q4 targets, a Slack channel. Sources, destination, deadline.

Output — exact format + thresholds. Slack summary by segment and rep. Coverage ratio. Commits ranked by ARR. Flag risks — low coverage, stale pipeline, deals stuck in the same stage.

Guardrails — scope first, then exclusions. New Business only. Commit and Best Case. Exclude inactive reps and deals past this quarter. Zero pipeline in a segment? Flag it, don't skip it.

You'll notice there's no role line. In Cowork, your project instructions already set that context — the role is handled before you even start typing. In Claude Chat, add "You are a RevOps analyst" before Intent.

Same ask. Completely different result.

Prompt structure is the thing nobody is teaching right now — but it's what separates AI that replaces a 3-hour process from AI that just generates more noise.

content:
Just spotted a new feature from Krisp: It can change your accent in real time during calls 🤯 (No I am not going to link this to B2B Sales or RevOps but its interesting)

Flip a switch → Go from an Indian accent to an American one 👀

Now on the surface → Its pretty wild tech. 

↳Could help non-native speakers get their point across better in high-stakes meetings.
↳Might reduce accent bias (which, let’s be honest, is still very real).
↳Useful in sales or support roles where clarity is key.

But it got me thinking...

↳Are we solving a communication problem or sidestepping a deeper cultural one?
↳Are we encouraging people to sound “more acceptable” to fit in?
↳Does this reinforce the very biases it’s meant to fix?

And what does this mean for authenticity?
 ↳Will it blur the line between real presence and polished AI personas? (half way there in this case imo)

Also curious about the tech side:
How well does it handle emotion and nuance?
Can it keep up with speed, humor, and local idioms?
Will global teams now skip learning to understand each other’s accents?

My take?

It’s both fascinating and a slippery slope.

Curious to hear your thoughts → Would you use something like this?
